about: M2-3 parity script for the device-pairing access requests. The same steps run against the host's real code (serve/host/src/remote/cloud.rs, test `access_request_parity_script`) and against the core's rows (core/runtime/src/authority/tests/requests.rs). Steps: file (a request arrives: id, device number, platform, person = a member or null for the owner, code = the device has shown its code), suspend (the owner suspends the person: the host moves their memberships to suspended_*, the core runs people.suspend), membership_gone (the cloud reports the membership gone while the person stays in kith-auth: the host removes the membership row and, on its membership sync, denies that person's pending requests, which the core is told with people.deny; since M2-17 both sides refuse and there is no known difference), sync (the host's membership sync after a suspend: it denies the pending requests of a person with no membership, which the core is told with people.deny; since M2-17 a suspension also ends the waiting requests, with either switch, so an undo afterwards does not bring them back), undo (the owner undoes the suspension: the host restores the memberships, the core runs people.undo), expire (the cloud stops listing it: the host drops it on its next pull, the core's clock passes expires_at), approve / deny (with the answer both must give), list (the ids the owner sees, oldest first). An error is the text both give.
